candidate_state: planned from the locally verified release candidate

internal_measurement.evaluator: material-only release validation; no new evaluator adopted
internal_measurement.results: Workspace release build, workspace checks, rustfmt, the 98% Rust coverage gate, a native material-only USI smoke, and local WebAssembly package generation passed before publication. Opt-in Lazy SMP diagnostics now distinguish confirmed worker-local and foreign-worker TT reuse and discarded root work without changing the default search policy. Match-runner process cleanup, bounded WebAssembly evaluator loading, and bounded MultiPV contracts are included. No general playing-strength claim is made.

external_opponents.configuration: No external engine, evaluator, weights, labels, Suisho5-derived scores, or Suisho5-derived opening positions are used as release evidence for v0.3.73.

known_limitations: No new NNUE checkpoint is bundled or adopted, and this release makes no general playing-strength claim.
Lazy SMP useful-work counters are opt-in diagnostics with sampling and relaxed atomic overhead; counter-enabled runs are not NPS baselines.
The four-thread LazyFlags vote candidate stopped INCONCLUSIVE at 28 wins, 38 losses, and 2 draws with LLR -0.33, so no playing default changed.
The optional v0.3.38 checkpoint and the default material evaluator remain unchanged.
Parallel search can vary by scheduler; deterministic diagnostics require one thread and SpecTopN=0.
The WebAssembly package is distributed as a GitHub Release asset and is not published to the npm registry.
External HalfKP inference remains optional and requires a separately obtained, license-compatible nn.bin file with its own provenance and operating scale.
